title: Unify stream cursor abstraction, auth handshake, and backoff across Python/TS/Go SDKs; cross-sdk version bumps
author: Leah Martinez
release_notes: Unified stream cursor API across Python/TS/Go, consistent auth handshake and exponential backoff defaults; ergonomics improvements for streaming loops; bumped SDK versions: python 2.8.0, typescript 1.12.0, go 0.9.0. No runtime-breaking changes expected; minor API surface tweaks documented in migration notes.
description:
Motivation: We have multiple inconsistent streaming iterator semantics, token-refresh handshakes, and backoff defaults across the Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs. This has caused developer confusion and subtle production bugs (lost partial messages on reconnect, token race during refresh) across customer integrations. This PR unifies the behaviour by introducing a common "StreamCursor"/iterator abstraction and standardizing the auth handshake lifecycle and retry/backoff defaults across the three SDKs.

What this PR does (high level): - Adds a StreamCursor abstraction in each SDK that provides: next()/has_next() style iteration, resume tokens for safe reconnects, and deterministic finalization to drain KV caches. - Implements a two-step auth handshake: (1) token pinning at stream open to avoid mid-stream rotation races, (2) transparent refresh callback with optimistic retry on auth failure. - Replaces per-language ad-hoc backoff constants with a shared policy: jittered exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max 8s, max retries 6 for transient stream errors. - Surfaces ergonomic helpers for common patterns: stream.to_async_iterator() in Python, stream.asyncIterable() in TS, and StreamCursor.Iter() in Go. - Updates examples, tests, and bump package versions in each SDK.

Files changed (high level): see changed_files for exact paths.

Migration notes: - Existing streaming loops that relied on the old per-chunk callback shape should switch to the StreamCursor API. Migration helpers are provided and are backwards-compatible wrappers for the most common patterns. - If you have custom token rotation, review the new refresh callback hook; handlers that mutate tokens should be idempotent and accept a context param in Go / cancellation token in TS / timeout in Python. - The default backoff is more aggressive than some client-customized configs; customers can override via the SDK config object (see examples).

Testing and QA: - Added cross-language unit and integration tests that validate partial message resume across disconnects and token rotation scenarios. - Ran full e2e matrix on linux/arm and linux/x86, and verified memory profiles for long-running streams. - Security scan: no new secrets; auth handshake code reviewed by security.

Checklist: - [x] Python implementation + tests + docs - [x] TypeScript implementation + tests + docs - [x] Go implementation + tests + docs - [x] Migration guides updated - [x] Bumped package versions and changelogs - [x] CI green (see ci_checks)

Related: ENG-3412 (stream reliability), ENG-3571 (sdk ergonomics), SUP-9182 (customer incident tied to token rotation).

review_comments: Daniel Park: This looks great overall. Two asks: 1) can we make the default backoff configurable from the top-level client config? 2) add a short benchmark (latency/throughput) for the new cursor to confirm no perf regression.

Leah Martinez: +1 on making backoff configurable. Added ClientConfig.streamBackoff and documented override in migration guide. Benchmarks added under benchmark-lab/examples/stream-cursor. See commit f6ea4b2.

Sandeep Rao: In Go StreamCursor.Iter(), the Close behavior needs to guarantee KV cache flush on error. Add an explicit Flush() call or document guarantee. Also prefer context-aware token refresh signature.
Leah Martinez: Addressed: added FlushOnClose boolean and ensured Flush() is called in the defer path. Token refresh now accepts context.Context. See go commit b4a7c33 (handshake.go updated).
Maya Chen: Minor nit: TS exported type name is StreamCursor but file is streamCursor.ts — can we align casing in package docs?
Leah Martinez: Renamed export to export type StreamCursor and added note in README.
